imprintomeR Command-Line Workflows

Source: vignettes/articles/command-line.Rmd
command-line.Rmd

This guide describes the package-installed command-line scripts for running methylation QC and imprinting analysis with imprintomeR.

The two scripts, run_meth_QC.R and run_imprintomeR.R, live in inst/scripts/ of the source package and are installed into the scripts/ folder of the installed package. Locate that folder once per shell session; the examples below use $SCRIPTS:

unset R_HOME
SCRIPTS=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts", package = "imprintomeR"))')
[ -n "$SCRIPTS" ] || echo "imprintomeR is not installed for this Rscript" >&2
echo "$SCRIPTS"    # e.g. ~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3/imprintomeR/scripts

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_meth_QC.R --help
Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R --help

system.file() returns an empty string when imprintomeR is not installed for the Rscript on your PATH; on a cluster, load the same R module you installed the package with. To run the scripts from a source checkout instead, set SCRIPTS=/path/to/imprintomeR/inst/scripts.

Workflow Overview

  1. Run run_meth_QC.R on raw IDAT files to create a MethQcSet and QC output files.
  2. Run run_imprintomeR.R on the QC RDS, or on beta plus metadata files, to create an ImprintomeSet, run imprinting analysis, save plot PDFs, and export result tables.

The recommended end-to-end workflow is:

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_meth_QC.R \
  -m metadata.tsv \
  -o qc_results \
  --platform EPIC \
  -v

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --probeset selected \
  --plot-types default \
  -v

Step 1: Methylation QC CLI

run_meth_QC.R processes IDAT files and exports a MethQcSet object plus QC tables and plots. By default, it also writes beta-density PDFs from the MethQcSet beta matrix and raw minfi density PDFs from minfi::qcReport() for all, PASS, and FAIL samples.

Inputs

Metadata should be TSV or CSV and include:

Column Required Notes
Sample_Name Yes Unique sample identifier.
SAMPLE_NAME Backward compatible Accepted and normalized to Sample_Name.
Basename Yes Full absolute IDAT path prefix, excluding Red.idat and Grn.idat.
Sample_Group Recommended Added automatically if missing.

IDAT files should use minfi-compatible names:

<Basename>_Red.idat
<Basename>_Grn.idat

Compressed .idat.gz files are accepted. Lowercase *_red.idat / *_green.idat files are renamed to *_Red.idat / *_Grn.idat when needed.

Basic QC Run 

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_meth_QC.R \
  -m metadata.tsv \
  -o qc_results

Useful QC Options

Option Default Description
--platform auto-detect Override platform detection: EPIC, EPICv2, 450K, or 27K.
--pcutoff / -p 0.05 Detection p-value threshold used for Final.QC: a sample passes when at least 95% of probes are detected at p < this value (and the bisulfite conversion I controls pass).
--icutoff / -i 11 Reference line for intensity plots only. Low intensity no longer fails Final.QC.
--plot-types intensity,detection_pval,probe_coverage,beta_density QC plots: intensity, detection_pval, probe_coverage, qc_bar, beta_density, or all.
--no-qc-plots FALSE Suppress QC plot generation.
--no-qc-report FALSE Suppress default QC report PDFs: root review PDFs plus secondary reports in plots/.
--normalization noob Beta normalization: noob, noob_swan, or raw (unnormalized, as in earlier versions). Recorded in qc_params(qcset)$normalization.
--skip-ewastools FALSE Deprecated and ignored: the control-probe, contamination and donor checks are built in and no longer use ewastools.
--verbose / -v FALSE Print detailed progress messages.

QC Outputs

For an EPIC run, the output directory typically contains:

qc_results/
+-- epic/
|   +-- epic_summary.txt
|   +-- epic_qc_table_main.xlsx
|   +-- epic_QC_detection_pval.pdf         # default root review plot
|   +-- epic_QC_probe_coverage.pdf         # default root review plot
|   +-- epic_QC_minfiDensity_all.pdf       # default root minfi density report
|   +-- data/
|   |   +-- epic_qcset.rds
|   |   +-- epic_beta.txt
|   |   +-- epic_meta.txt
|   +-- QC_tables/
|   |   +-- epic_qc_table_extra.xlsx
|   |   +-- epic_qc_matrix.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_statistics.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_recall_rate.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_cutoffs.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_ctrl_metrics.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_contamination.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_predUniqDonor_ID.txt
|   |   +-- epic_qc_qc_report_files.txt
|   +-- plots/
|       +-- epic_QC_intensity.pdf
|       +-- epic_QC_betaDensity_all.pdf    # cache-friendly
|       +-- epic_QC_betaDensity_pass.pdf   # cache-friendly
|       +-- epic_QC_betaDensity_fail.pdf   # if FAIL samples exist
|       +-- epic_QC_minfiDensity_pass.pdf  # fresh IDAT QC only
|       +-- epic_QC_minfiDensity_fail.pdf  # fresh IDAT QC only, if FAIL samples exist
|       +-- qc_intensity.png
|       +-- qc_detection_pval.png
|       +-- qc_probe_coverage.png
|       +-- qc_beta_density.png
+-- run_meth_QC.log

The complete QC object is saved as data/{platform}_qcset.rds, for example:

qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds

run_meth_QC.R reuses this cached RDS only when it is a MethQcSet, the platform matches, and the cached Sample_Name set matches the current metadata. PNG QC plots and beta-density PDFs can be regenerated from cache. Raw minfi density PDFs require IDAT reload; remove the cached RDS to force a full rerun when {platform}_QC_minfiDensity_*.pdf files are needed. If the script warns that runMethQC() does not support density-report output, reinstall/update imprintomeR so the loaded package version matches the CLI script.

Step 2: Imprintome Analysis CLI

run_imprintomeR.R runs post-QC imprinting analysis. It can start from either a MethQcSet RDS or beta plus metadata files.

Recommended Input: MethQcSet RDS 

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --probeset selected \
  -v

When Final.QC is available in the MethQcSet, the runner keeps QC-pass samples using:

qcset_pass <- subsetMethQC(qcset, final_qc = "PASS")

If no sample has Final.QC == "PASS", the script stops.

Alternative Input: Beta and Metadata Files 

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -b /data/beta.txt \
  -m /data/meta.txt \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix beta_run \
  --probeset selected

The beta matrix should have probes as rows and samples as columns. Metadata should contain Sample_Name; Sample_Group is preferred.

Useful Analysis Options

Option Default Description
--rds / -r NA Input MethQcSet RDS file.
--beta-file / -b NA Beta matrix file, required unless --rds is used.
--meta-file / -m NA Metadata file, required unless --rds is used.
--outdir / -o required Output directory.
--prefix / -p basename of outdir Dataset prefix for result, plot, and RDS filenames; the normalized genome is appended automatically.
--probeset selected One of selected, NanoImprint, Joshi, Court, Rosenski, Jima, chr11p15, chr20q13.
--plot-types default Comma-separated plot types, default, or all.
--ids-cutoff 0.2 IDS cutoff passed to runImprintome().
--genome hg38 Genome build for bundled probesets (hg19 or hg38). Also used in output file names.
--dmr-type panel default DMR types to score: all, or comma-separated DMR_type values such as gametic or secondary. The selected panel is scored on gametic ICRs by default; other panels on all probes.
--reference-group none Comma-separated Sample_Group value(s) used as in-cohort controls: each probe’s reference becomes the controls’ median beta (controls scored leave-one-out).
--reference-file none External control reference: a beta matrix file or an .rds from BuildReferenceProfile(). Without controls, the fixed 0.5 reference is used.
--infinium-type all Infinium design types to score: all, I, II, or balanced (deviations computed within type I and type II probes and averaged).
--balance probe Pooling for the sample-level IDS: probe (median over probes) or icr (median within each ICR, then across ICRs).
--n-boot 0 Bootstrap replicates (0 = off; 1000–2000 for reporting). Adds IDS_lower, IDS_upper, Angle_lower, Angle_upper, Mechanism_support and Status_interval (above cutoff, below cutoff or borderline).
--resample icr Bootstrap scheme: icr (ICRs, then probes within ICRs) or probe. Panels with one ICR per parental class (chr11p15) resample probes.
--resample-reference FALSE Also resample the controls in each replicate (needs --reference-group).
--n-perm 0 Permutations for the origin test (origin_perm_p); needs a control reference.
--permute icr Permutation unit for the origin test: icr or probe. When not given, panels with one ICR per parental class (such as chr11p15) fall back to probe, with a warning.
--conf-level 0.95 Confidence level of the bootstrap intervals.
--seed random Random seed; when none is given one is drawn and written to run_imprintomeR.log.
--all-probes FALSE Load every probe of --beta-file. By default only probes of the bundled panels are read, so genome-wide beta files need little memory.
--icr FALSE Also score each ICR (AnalyzeICRStatus()) and write the per-ICR table, its per-sample multi-locus summary and, with the default or all plot set, the per-ICR heatmap (icr_heatmap).
--skip-plots FALSE Skip the ordinary plot workflow; explicit --rainfall-all, --radar-all, and --beeswarm-chr-all outputs still run.
--rainfall-all NULL Pass TRUE to generate one multipage rainfall PDF containing every sample.
--radar-all NULL Pass TRUE to generate one multipage radar PDF containing every sample.
--beeswarm-chr-all NULL Pass TRUE to generate one multipage chromosome-beeswarm PDF containing every sample.
--verbose / -v FALSE Print detailed progress messages.

Plot Types

--plot-types default uses the standard workflow plot set from runImprintomeVisualizations():

  • polar
  • beeswarm_origin
  • mirror_density
  • heatmap_by_probe
  • heatmap_by_gene
  • radar
  • beeswarm_chr
  • rainfall
  • icr_heatmap (with --icr): samples × ICRs heatmap of the per-ICR deviations (PlotICRHeatmap()); non-gametic ICRs are marked with *

circular_heatmap is not included in default. Request it explicitly when needed:

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --plot-types circular_heatmap

--plot-types all includes all supported plot types, including circular_heatmap, beeswarm, violin, and cor_heatmap.

Plots are saved directly as PDF files and are not embedded in the exported ImprintomeSet RDS. This keeps the cached RDS smaller.

Rainfall Plots For All Samples

Pass --rainfall-all TRUE to generate one multipage rainfall PDF with one 12 x 6 inch page per sample:

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --probeset selected \
  --rainfall-all TRUE

When enabled, the ordinary single-sample rainfall entry is removed from the regular plot workflow. All-sample rainfall generation is explicit and independent of --skip-plots. The PDF is written directly under the output directory as <prefix>_<genome>_rainfall.<probeset>.all.pdf. Omitting --rainfall-all preserves the existing single-sample rainfall behavior.

Radar Plots For All Samples

Pass --radar-all TRUE to generate one multipage radar PDF with one page per sample. Radar plots have one spoke per curated ICR, in genomic order clockwise from the top, labelled chromosome_annotated parental origin_ICR; the page size grows with the label length (about 17 x 17 inches for the selected panel) so that no label is clipped:

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --probeset selected \
  --radar-all TRUE

When enabled, the ordinary single-sample radar entry is removed from the regular plot workflow. All-sample radar generation is explicit and independent of --skip-plots. The PDF is written directly under the output directory as <prefix>_<genome>_radar.<probeset>.all.pdf. Omitting --radar-all preserves the existing single-sample radar behavior.

Single-sample rainfall and radar files use <prefix>_<genome>_rainfall.<probeset>.<sampleID>.pdf and <prefix>_<genome>_radar.<probeset>.<sampleID>.pdf, respectively.

Chromosome Beeswarm For All Samples

Pass --beeswarm-chr-all TRUE to generate one multipage PDF with one 10 x 4 inch page per sample:

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE166531 \
  --probeset chr11p15 \
  --beeswarm-chr-all TRUE

When enabled, the ordinary single-sample beeswarm_chr entry is removed from the regular plot workflow. Multipage generation is explicit and independent of --skip-plots. The PDF is written directly under the output directory as <prefix>_<genome>_beeswarm_chr.<probeset>.all.pdf.

Each page shows only chromosomes with at least five usable (finite) probe values for that sample.

Per-ICR Scores

The sample-level IDS pools all probes of a parental class, so a defect at one ICR or on one chromosome changes it little. Add --icr to also score each ICR on its own and summarize the altered ICRs per sample:

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r qc_results/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o imprintome_results \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --probeset selected \
  --reference-group control \
  --icr \
  -v

--icr writes, in addition to the sample-level table:

  • <prefix>_<genome>_results_ICRStatus.<probeset>.tsv: one row per sample and ICR, with the deviation, z, the altered call, and the ICR’s annotated parental origin and DMR_type;
  • <prefix>_<genome>_results_ICRSummary.<probeset>.tsv: per sample, the numbers of altered ICRs (gains and losses), the chromosomes involved and the multi-locus (MLID) flag;
  • <prefix>_<genome>_icr_heatmap.<probeset>.pdf: samples by ICRs heatmap of the deviations, drawn with --plot-types default or all (or alone with --plot-types icr_heatmap); non-gametic ICRs are marked with *.

An ICR is called altered when |deviation| ≥ 0.175 and |z| ≥ 2 against the controls. These thresholds were validated with control samples: give in-cohort controls with --reference-group or an external reference with --reference-file. Without controls, z is unavailable, only the deviation criterion applies and the calls are exploratory. Per-ICR scores cover all annotated ICRs, secondary DMRs included; --dmr-type changes only the sample-level score.

--balance icr is a separate option: it computes the sample-level IDS/Angle with each ICR counted once (median within each ICR, then across ICRs). It can be combined with --icr.

Bootstrap intervals and the origin test are added with --n-boot and --n-perm, for example --reference-group control --n-boot 2000 --resample-reference --n-perm 2000 --seed 1. The run log records the package version, the arguments and the seed.

The per-ICR thresholds (delta_cutoff, z_cutoff) and restricting per-ICR scores to gametic ICRs (dmr_type = "gametic") are available from R, through runImprintome(), AnalyzeICRStatus() and SummarizeICRStatus(), but not as command-line options.

Imprintome Outputs

A typical analysis directory (default --genome hg38) contains:

imprintome_results/
+-- run_imprintomeR.log
+-- GSE240091_hg38_imprintomeSet.rds
+-- GSE240091_hg38_results_AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.tsv
+-- GSE240091_hg38_results_ICRStatus.selected.tsv     (--icr)
+-- GSE240091_hg38_results_ICRSummary.selected.tsv    (--icr)
+-- GSE240091_hg38_polar.selected.pdf
+-- GSE240091_hg38_heatmap_by_gene.selected.pdf
+-- GSE240091_hg38_icr_heatmap.selected.pdf          (--icr)
+-- GSE240091_hg38_radar.<probeset>.<sample_id>.pdf
+-- GSE240091_hg38_rainfall.<probeset>.<sample_id>.pdf

With --genome hg19 the names use _hg19_ instead. Runs made before the default changed to hg38 wrote _hg19_ files; pass --genome hg19 to reuse those cached results.

The main result table is stored as AnalyzeImprintStatus.<probeset> inside results(x) and exported as a genome-prefixed TSV file.

Example reload:

library(imprintomeR)
x <- readRDS("imprintome_results/GSE240091_hg38_imprintomeSet.rds")
names(results(x))
status <- results(x)[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected"]]

Imprintome RDS Cache Behavior

The runner saves a lean object as:

<prefix>_<genome>_imprintomeSet.rds

The object contains beta values, metadata, probeset data, and result tables, but not stored plot objects.

The same dataset and genome share this RDS across probesets. Different genomes use separate cache files. On later runs:

  • If the cached RDS contains AnalyzeImprintStatus.<probeset> with matching genome and --ids-cutoff provenance, analysis is skipped and requested plot/result files are regenerated without overwriting the RDS.
  • If the requested probeset result is absent, or its stored --ids-cutoff differs, core analysis is rerun for that probeset and the lean RDS is updated. Recalculation replaces that probeset’s prior result while preserving other named probeset results.
  • Plot PDFs are generated directly and are not saved back into the RDS.

End-to-End Example For HPC 

module load R/4.2.2

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_meth_QC.R \
  -m GSE240091_metadata.tsv \
  -b GSE240091_raw/idats \
  -o GSE240091_qc \
  --platform EPIC \
  --plot-types all \
  -v

Rscript "$SCRIPTS"/run_imprintomeR.R \
  -r GSE240091_qc/epic/data/epic_qcset.rds \
  -o GSE240091_imprintome \
  --prefix GSE240091 \
  --probeset selected \
  --plot-types default \
  -v

Troubleshooting

imprintomeR package not found

Install the package into the R library used by the job or Jupyter kernel:

install.packages("/path/to/imprintomeR", repos = NULL, type = "source")

IDAT files not found

Check Basename. It must be a full absolute IDAT path prefix.

No samples with Final.QC == "PASS"

The imprintome runner stops because there are no QC-clean samples to analyze. Review qc_tables(qcset)$QC_matrix from the QC stage.

Plot PDFs are missing

Run with --verbose and try a smaller plot set first:

--plot-types polar,heatmap_by_gene

Some plots require enough samples, enough probes, or metadata columns such as Sample_Group.

Quick Output Checklist

After QC:

qc_results/<platform>/data/<platform>_qcset.rds
qc_results/<platform>/<platform>_qc_table_main.xlsx
qc_results/<platform>/plots/

After imprintome analysis:

imprintome_results/<prefix>_<genome>_imprintomeSet.rds
imprintome_results/<prefix>_<genome>_results_AnalyzeImprintStatus.<probeset>.tsv
imprintome_results/<prefix>_<genome>_<plot_name>.pdf
imprintome_results/<prefix>_<genome>_rainfall.<probeset>.all.pdf
imprintome_results/<prefix>_<genome>_radar.<probeset>.all.pdf
imprintome_results/<prefix>_<genome>_beeswarm_chr.<probeset>.all.pdf
